saints.name: St. Paul the Hermit
saints.title: Hermit
saints.shortBlurb: The first Christian hermit, who fled to the Egyptian desert and lived there alone for some ninety years…
biography: Paul of Thebes, honored as the first Christian hermit, was born about 227 in the Lower Thebaid of Egypt. About 250, when the persecution of Decius broke out and his own brother-in-law plotted to betray him, he fled toward the Red Sea and found a cave beside a spring and a palm tree, which gave him water, dates, and clothing.

There, according to the life written by Jerome, he remained in solitude for some ninety years, a raven bringing him half a loaf each day. In his last years Anthony of Egypt, told in a dream of a hermit holier than himself, sought him out; that day the raven brought a whole loaf, and the two old men ate and spoke together.

Paul died soon after, about 341, being one hundred and thirteen years old by Jerome's reckoning; Anthony found him dead at prayer and buried him in the cloak that Athanasius had given him, two lions digging the grave. The Order of Saint Paul the First Hermit, founded in thirteenth-century Hungary, still bears his name.
saints.knownFor: Being the first of the Christian hermits.
